title: Edge-case go-live pulse and incident bootplan
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact roadmap tracker + KPI sheet focused on low-probability/high-impact edge cases for upcoming launches, and an incident bootplan tied to the go/no-go signals. Intended audience: product-ops, SRE, release-engineering, and on-call leads.

Scope: 
- Launch: incremental rollout v0.9 -> v1.0 to customers in NA region, Stage: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic.
- Focus: edge-case behavior (cache storms, long-tail latency during prefix-heavy workloads, KV cache eviction regressions, fallback model degradations).
- Timebox: preflight checks 72–24 hours prior; canary day, ramp day, and 3-day post-ramp watch.

Quick timeline (high level):
- T-72h: Final baked-in telemetry and extra debug hooks enabled for canary. Owners: Diego (telemetry), Priya (canary config).
- T-48h: Dry-run smoke with synthetic traffic (prefix variants). Record baseline KPIs. Owner: Elliot.
- T-24h: Stakeholder sync, final contingency signoff, runbook reviewed. Owner: Maya.
- Canary day: Deploy to canary fleet (5% dynamic). Monitor pulse signals for 6h before next ramp.
- Ramp increments: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 2h pause windows and criteria evaluation.

KPI tracker (single-line rows for spreadsheet conversion):
- KPI:99p-latency-ms | Target: < 220 ms | Canary-baseline: 180 ms | Gate: must not increase > 20% | Owner: SRE-oncall
- KPI:median-latency-ms | Target: < 90 ms | Canary-baseline: 72 ms | Gate: none (informational) | Owner: SRE
- KPI:token-cost-per-1k | Target: <= $0.95 | Baseline: $0.86 | Gate: cost > 10% triggers billing review | Owner: Finance-ops
- KPI:prediction-divergence-rate | Target: < 1.5% lift vs baseline | Canary-baseline: 0.6% | Gate: >1% regression => hold and investigate | Owner: Applied-ML
- KPI:cache-miss-rate-prefix | Target: < 8% | Baseline: 4.1% | Gate: > 12% => investigate cache policies | Owner: Serving-runtime
- KPI:error-rate-5xx | Target: < 0.2% | Baseline: 0.05% | Gate: >= 0.5% => immediate rollback consideration | Owner: SRE/oncall

Traffic & capacity quick numbers (estimates):
- Expected steady RPS at 100%: 1,400 RPS (peak 2,100 RPS)
- Canary RPS (5%): 70 RPS; 10%: 140 RPS; 50%: 700 RPS
- GPU pool sizing: reserved 18 GPUs for serving runtime (mixed A100/RTX mix), burst pool +8 GPUs 
- KV cache capacity headroom: baseline 85% utilization expected during spikes, plan to enable prefix pooling if >90%

Gating criteria (Go/No-Go quick rubric):
- Safety gates (auto-fail => rollback): 5xx error rate sustained above gate threshold for >5m OR latency P99 > 2x baseline for >10m.
- Quality gates (manual hold): prediction-divergence increases >1% AND customer-visible complaints within 1h.
- Cost gates (escalate): sustained token-cost-per-1k > 15% above baseline for >30m.
- Observability gates: missing telemetry or degraded sampling rate - NO GO until fixed.

Contingency and incident bootplan (edge-case focus):
- Signal: abrupt P99 jump with minimal 5xx increase (likely tail latency or blocking kernel).
  - Step 1: Flip debug sampling to 100% for affected routes (Diego).
  - Step 2: Isolate model variant routing (switch to lower-memory quantized variant) using smart routing fallback (Priya).
  - Step 3: Throttle non-critical background requests and reduce batch window (Elliot).
  - Step 4: If P99 not recovering in 15m, initiate canary rollback to previous model build and reduce traffic to 20%.
- Signal: cache storm (high miss rate, KV eviction spikes).
  - Step 1: Temporarily disable prefix grouping to stop noisy sharding (Serving-runtime).
  - Step 2: Enable cold-warm cache lane and increase cache TTL for frequent prefixes.
  - Step 3: Engage infra to add read-only replicas if read latency spike persists.
- Signal: model-quality drift on subset of prompts (prediction-divergence).
  - Step 1: Pause rollout, snapshot offending prompts to S3, tag as regression test cases.
  - Step 2: Trigger A/B rollback or route to conservative fallback model.
  - Step 3: Notify product and CS for early customer outreach.

On-call responsibilities & communication plan:
- Primary oncall (SRE): monitor KPIs and act on auto-fail gates; escalate to release-engineering slack #release-control within 5 minutes of gate breach.
- Product-ops (Maya): coordinate stakeholder updates and customer comms; maintain the rollforward/rollback decision log.
- Release-engineering: own deploy and rollback actions; maintain deployment artifacts and PR links.
- Communication channels: #release-control (public ops), private channel #release-control-priv for legal/enterprise customers during escalations.
- Status updates cadence: every 15 minutes during canary, every 30 minutes during ramp, ad-hoc on incidents.

Preflight checklist (72–0 hrs):
- [ ] Extra telemetry flags enabled and smoke dashboards created (Diego).
- [ ] Synthetic prefix traffic run completed and baseline recorded (Elliot).
- [ ] Canary config validated with rollout window and pause timings (Priya).
- [ ] Runbook reviewed with oncall and ENG leads (Maya).
- [ ] Customer-facing rollback notice prepared for enterprise customers (GTM lead).
- [ ] Billing alert threshold configured (Finance-ops).
- [ ] Security review signoff for new key/materials if any (Security & Compliance).

Post-launch 72-hour watch and required artifacts:
- Postmortem checklist: capture timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation scope, tickets created, lessons learned.
- Required logs & artifacts to collect: sampling flamegraphs, kernel tracer outputs, model logits for flagged requests, KV cache eviction histograms.
- Post-launch metrics to publish (public digest): mean P99 latency delta, error-rate curve, cost delta per 1k tokens, small-sample annotation accuracy on regression set.

Open questions / risk notes (quick bullets):
- Are we comfortable with burst capacity peg of +8 GPUs given cloud quota limits in region? (Action: finance/infra to confirm by T-48h).
- If fallback model has different tokenization, do we need adapter layer for client calls? (Action: serving-runtime & devx).
- Is CS prepared with canned messages for early adopters if we route to fallback? (Action: CS runbook).

Sign-off block (for final readiness):
- Release-engineering lead (name): ____________________  Date: _____
- SRE oncall lead: ____________________  Date: _____
- Product-ops (Maya Thompson): ____________________  Date: _____
- Security/compliance: ____________________  Date: _____

Notes to self (working doc style):
- Keep this file as the single-source mini-playbook for edge-case handling; make small updates and stamp with last_modified.
- After first ramp, convert key gating thresholds into automated dashboards and 1-click actions where safe.

Attachments and references: Confluence runbook page (linked_artifacts), Jira PROD-3421 (linked_artifacts), PR for release notes (linked_artifacts).

End of working doc.
summary: Compact working doc for a go-live focused on edge-case detection and incident bootplan; includes timeline, KPI gates, capacity estimates, preflight checklist, runbook steps, sign-off template.
